summary: The government of Finland has announced it will offer, via the European Union, to send three specialist firefighting helicopters, 25 firefighters and 2–3 forest fire experts to Greece to assist with the current forest fire emergency, and said they would be dispatched within six hours of Greece requesting the rotorcraft and personnel if the offers are deemed suitable. Greece is in urgent need of fixed-wing water-bombing aircraft, which Finland does not possess; Finland's helicopters, sourced via a private company, can each carry up to 800 litres of water or foam retardant compared with tens of thousands of litres carried by large firefighting planes, and Finland said it could not commit to send the aircraft any sooner without arrangements to cover their removal from service because that would jeopardise safety in Finland. The personnel would most likely be used to protect built-up areas to try to prevent the death toll, already over 60, from rising further, and Finland had previously thought it could not spare help until private-sector sourcing made the offer possible and is also looking into whether it may assist with reforestation after the fires are extinguished.
